summary: Complete the per-channel DAC->parameter mapping (voice engine)
description: DONE (reviewed 2026-10-07): all ten DAC-driven CEM3396 inputs mapped to patch parameter, compiler, store primitive, voice-block pointer and channel address. Method: each element compiler ($95AB..$992F) stores a matrix destination code 1-12 in $7220, reads its patch parameter from the active patch ($7218=$7A19, indexed by parameter number) and emits one store primitive ($8950..$8D1B); each primitive does LDX <ptr to a channel cached at boot ($80D8-$8146, plus the 18-byte-per-voice $8220 table). Map: DCO1 shape $1000, DCO1 PW $1006, DCO2 shape $100E, DCO2 PW $100A, VCA1 $1004, VCA2 $1008, VCF FM $108C, VCF freq $1102 (all +n*$10), resonance $106C+2n, mix $1160+2n; pulse-off variants write PW offset +$80. Pitch (dest 1/4) is the 8253 path. Cross-checked against the CEM3396 datasheet: wave-select (pin 6) is a logic-driven input, leaving exactly 10 DAC CVs; waveshape CV is scaled by a pitch factor and PW by the waveshape CV, as the datasheet requires; the $3C80 pitch-range flag drives per-DCO Rt range latches $1C00+n/$1C80+n. Also found: boot write of raw $8000 to $1008+n*$10 is VCA2=0 (mute), not a mid-scale settle; VCF freq and resonance use per-voice calibration data at voice +$2AA (9-point curve) and +$2A8. Written into docs/hardware/dac-cv-mux.md (Per-voice channel map), voice-engine.md, ram-map.md, io-map.md, voice-architecture.md, docs/README.md. NOT done (filed as #35): electrical decode of the address bits, DCO1=converter-A and VCA1=linear-pin confirmation, $107E wave-select. These need the schematic.

summary: Schematic-confirm the DAC address decode, pin assignments and $107E wave-select path
description: DONE (reviewed 2026-10-08): the DAC path is schematic-confirmed end to end, using Bob Grieb's redraw (pages 1, 4, 5) and Oberheim's own sheets (doc 2457 Rev B: sheet 3 DAC, sheet 11 Voice 6). (1) Address decode: the even-address DAC write latches the ADDRESS into U709 as the route: A1-A3 = mux channel (SHA/SHB/SHC), A4-A6 = which mux via U715 (SH1-6 = voices, SH7 = U701, SH8 = U702), A7 = RANGE1, A8 = RANGE2. Even byte bits 6-0 = DAC D1-D7, bit 7 = FASTb (active low); odd byte bits 7-3 = D8-D12, bit 2 = ENS&Hb (mux enable). So EORA #$80 is the FASTb inversion, not offset binary (corrected), and STA $1800 is not a mux strobe ($1800 = SWb panel read; corrected). (2) Per-voice 4051 ch0-7 = Wave A, Filter freq, log gain (pin 1), Pulse A, linear gain (pin 22), Pulse B, Filter mod, Wave B; matches every code-derived channel. DCO1 = converter A confirmed. VCA names are crossed: patch VCA1 (param 31) -> pin 1 log, patch VCA2 (envelope) -> pin 22 linear; Oberheim labels pin 22 'VCA1 (LIN)'. (3) Pulse-off +$80 = same channel and pin as PW, through RANGE1 (negative-going output, as the datasheet advises). Resonance/mix stride 2 = shared muxes U701 (BAL1-6, RES1-2) and U702 (RES3-6). (4) Fast path: second 4051 per voice gated by FASTb bypasses the 1M/0.0068uF smoothing; firmware flag voice +$0B set by source heads $9D9D/$9DB7/$9DED. (5) $1C00/$1C80 = 74HC259 addressable latches RA1-6/RB1-6 (Rt range); $1C06 = global noise enable (was 'LED latch'). Wave select is NOT $107E: it is global, bits 4-5 of $1D00 (74HC174 U705, also MUTE bit 1, SYNC2 bit 2, SYNC1 bit 3), built at $9529-$9587 via table $9594 ($20/$30/$10/$00) matching the datasheet's four levels. So wave enables, sync and noise are per patch, not per voice. Docs: dac-cv-mux.md rewritten; voice-architecture.md, io-map.md (DAC bits, $1800, $1C00/$1C80/$1C06/$1D00), panel-display.md, ram-map.md (+$0B, $7235), boot-init.md (MUTE), docs/README.md. NOT done (filed as #38): output voltage window of each RANGE; purpose of $107E and STA $1800.

summary: Analyse Tauntek v1.20 against v1.11: what the MIDI speed-ups changed
description: Tauntek (Bob Grieb) v1.20 is the most relevant prior art for the README section 6 'MIDI under load' limitation, and it was previously absent from our archive. Now held locally at reference/extracted/matrix-1000/os-rom/v1.20/mtrx1kv120.bin (md5 a8092cfa56189c5bb7c1775e7b4ca09b, dated 2016-01-13) with its ReadmeM1K.txt. Verified: 16-bit sum $21EC matches the readme; reset/IRQ/FIRQ vectors identical to v1.11 ($8003/$85E3/$84B4); 6552 of 32768 bytes differ from v1.11. Readme claims: MIDI parameter-change speed-ups, GliGli's detune code (with permission), parameter values written to the display on MIDI edit, NRPN inc/dec fix. Plan: diff against v1.11 at the routine level (changed byte runs mapped onto v1.11 labels in build/v111_full.asm), identify which routines were rewritten vs relocated, and document the MIDI-path changes against docs/firmware/midi-handling.md and the rebuild path in voice-engine.md / mod-matrix.md. Cross-check the detune piece against v1.16. Constraint: the image is third-party and not licensed for redistribution; describe its changes and cite addresses, do not copy code or bundle the binary.

summary: DAC output range voltages; explain the $107E and STA $1800 writes
description: Remainder of #35 (see docs/hardware/dac-cv-mux.md, sections 'Output ranges' and 'Wave select, sync and mute'). (1) Compute the DAC output voltage window for no range, RANGE1 (A7, adds a 182k resistor via U710) and RANGE2 (A8, swaps R726 133k for R724 20k) from the U706/U707 output stage on schematic page 4 (and Oberheim sheet 3). Expected: RANGE1 reaches slightly below 0 V (pulse off, VCF FM), RANGE2 spans roughly -2.5..+5 V (cutoff) and bipolar (mix). (2) $107E: written with $7213/$7214 by $9600/$9728 as a single even-address store; decodes to U702 channel 7, unconnected on both schematics. Purpose unknown (a 'park' of the mux route? leftover from Matrix-6 code?). Compare against the Matrix-6/6R firmware in reference/. (3) STA $1800 at $8995 (only in the DCO1 waveshape primitive): $1800 decodes to SWb, the panel switch read buffers. No documented effect.
